args.query: exchange gateway upstream timeout 503 partner exchange api
order submit 504 rollback did not recover error rate external provider

events.statement: order-service error_rate jumped from ~0.2% to ~31% starting in the 10:51 bucket and remained ~31% (last 30.39%, max 35.57%) through 12:45.
exchange-gateway logs show upstream connect timeouts to host=api.exchange-partner.example and 'exchange-api returned 503 Service Unavailable', first appearing at 11:01:25.
exchange-gateway error_rate rose from ~0.2% to ~44% starting in the 10:51 bucket and stayed elevated (last 46.67%) through 12:45.
exchange-gateway upstream_error_rate (calls to the partner) rose from ~0.3% to ~46% and upstream_latency_ms rose from ~120ms to ~9,200ms starting at the 10:51 bucket.
order-service ERROR logs are exclusively 'exchange-gateway call failed: 504 Gateway Timeout (placeOrder)', 349 total matches from 11:02:45 to 12:58:54.
order-service v2.15.2 was deployed 10:48 and rolled back at 11:16, yet error rate stayed ~31% until at least 12:45 (no recovery after rollback).
exchange-gateway logs include a WARN 'circuit breaker OPEN for exchange-api (failure ratio 0.47 over 60s)' at 11:03:26.
order-service depends on exchange-gateway (http) and exchange-gateway depends on external exchange-api (vendor, has_telemetry:false).
exchange-gateway CPU (~30%), memory (~44%), restarts (0) and request_rate (~270 req/s) all stayed flat across the incident onset; no local resource anomaly.
order-service db_pool_in_use stayed flat at ~14 connections and restarts stayed 0 throughout.
pricing-engine error_rate (~0.2%) and latency_p99_ms (~60ms) stayed flat throughout, and its only config change was a cache TTL 5->4s at 09:20.
ledger-db slow_queries_per_min stayed flat (~1/min) throughout, showing no database-side degradation.

The similarity of the current pattern to past incident HIST-103 ('Order failures during exchange partner outage', root_cause 'External exchange API outage on the partner side') supports a dependency-failure origin.
exchange-api (the external partner) has no telemetry available, so the partner-side failure cannot be directly observed from our data.
